title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 768-770 of the continuation of La Longue Marche): Grothendieck sets up a theory of fundamental groups for 'germes d'espaces'. A germ is a pair (S, 𝔏): a topological space S with a filter 𝔏 of (open) subsets. The category of coverings is Rev(S,𝔏) = 2-colim_{S_i∈𝔏} Rev(S_i). An object is a covering of some S_i, and morphisms are taken after shrinking. In modern terms this is the covering category of the pro-space (S_i)_{i}, so of a pro-object in spaces.

The previous page defines two notions.
- 0-connected: Ens → Rev(S,𝔏) is fully faithful. For S locally connected this means π0(S_j) → π0(S_i) is constant for suitable S_j ⊂ S_i.
- 1-connected: the constant-covering functor Ens → Rev(S,𝔏) is an equivalence. Equivalently, for each S_i there is a smaller S_j such that π1 of each component of S_j maps trivially to π1(S_i). In modern terms the pro-π1 is pro-trivial on coverings.

On this page:
(i) Coverings of germs form a category fibred over the category of germs. Top embeds fully in germs via X ↦ (X, trivial filter {X}). The fibred category of coverings of germs restricts to the usual coverings of spaces.
(ii) Let 𝔛 be a germ with Rev(𝔛) multigaloisian, i.e. a disjoint sum of categories of the form Ens(π). Let 𝔖 be a 1-connected germ and 𝔖 → 𝔛 a morphism of germs. Pullback gives Rev(𝔛) → Rev(𝔖) ≃ Ens (49), which is a fibre functor. This defines π1(𝔛, 𝔖) (50) as the automorphism group of that fibre functor.
(iii) If 𝔛 is connected (Rev galoisian), then Rev(𝔛) ≃ Ens(π) with π = π1(𝔛, 𝔖) (51, next page).

Next page: π1 is functorial in arrows 𝔖 → 𝔛 with 1-connected source. It introduces the germ of X along Y (neighbourhood filter) and the 'residual germ' (filter induced on X∖Y). The main case is Y = {x}: the local fundamental group of a punctured neighbourhood, as for a link of a singularity, or a group at infinity via X = S ∪ {ω}.

Purpose: a flexible notion of base point. Any 1-connected germ (a germ of a point, a sector at a puncture, a ray to infinity) can serve as base point. This gives fundamental groups of local and residual germs. In the Longue Marche setting it serves the Teichmüller/Galois-action study near the boundary and at punctures, where 'base points at infinity' are needed.
errors: Rev(𝔛) of a germ is a 2-colimit of Ens(π1(S_i)) along restriction. It is equivalent to Ens(π) for a single discrete group π only under a stability (essential constancy / Mittag-Leffler-type) condition on the pro-group (π1(S_i)). Otherwise one gets something like a pro-group action category. Grothendieck covers this by the hypothesis 'multigaloisienne' and the earlier remark 'dans les bons cas', so this is a hypothesis, not an error.

Next page: 'the germ of X at x is trivially 1-connected'. Essential surjectivity is indeed automatic, since coverings are locally trivial. But full faithfulness (0-connectedness) requires some local connectedness at x. For non-locally-connected points (e.g. comb-type spaces) the germ need not be 0-connected, so 'trivially' needs that hypothesis.

The previous page's criterion for 1-connectedness (π1 maps trivial) is sufficient but somewhat stronger than needed for coverings alone, for spaces that are not semi-locally simply connected. This is minor.

ideas.what: Germs of spaces (S, filter 𝔏) and their covering category as a 2-colimit; spaces embedded fully via the trivial filter
ideas.modern_name: covering theory of pro-spaces / pro-objects; shape-theoretic fundamental pro-group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pro-objects: Grothendieck (SGA4); shape theory: Borsuk (1968), Mardešić–Segal; étale homotopy of pro-objects: Artin–Mazur
ideas.where_published: Pro-objects in SGA4 / SGA1-style Galois categories. This topological 'germe d'espaces' formalism has not been located in published texts.

ideas.what: Fundamental group with base 'point' an arbitrary 1-connected germ 𝔖 → 𝔛, defined via the fibre functor Rev(𝔛) → Rev(𝔖) ≃ Ens, functorial in such arrows
ideas.modern_name: generalized / tangential base points (base point given by a simply connected germ, e.g. a sector at a puncture)

ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (base points 'à l'infini'); unsure of the explicit formulation

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates base points as arbitrary 1-connected germs mapping to a germ of space and defines π1(𝔛, 𝔖) functorially in such arrows. This is a topological, general-shape precursor of tangential base points, written in the Longue Marche continuation (c. 1981). That predates Deligne's 1989 introduction, and here it is embedded in a germ / pro-space framework that also yields local and 'at infinity' groups uniformly.
missed.quote: soit 𝔖 un germe d'espace 1-connexe, 𝔖 → 𝔛 un morphisme. Alors on a Rev(𝔛) → Rev(𝔖) ≃ (Ens) foncteur fibre ... définir π1(𝔛, 𝔖)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to crediting tangential base points and to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, which uses 'base points at infinity' for braid/mapping class groupoids. The general germ formalism unifies tangential base points, local π1 of singularities and π1 at infinity in one functorial setting.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is a clean but mostly routine setup: a covering theory of filtered (pro-)spaces in Galois-category language. The one notable point is the systematic use of 1-connected germs as generalized base points, a topological form of tangential base points, apparently a few years before Deligne. Its priority value is modest, since related ideas of 'base points at infinity' are associated with Grothendieck's Longue Marche/Esquisse circle anyway.
transcription_corrections: 'genres d'espaces' should read 'germes d'espaces' throughout, as on the next page ('germes d'espaces'). The handwriting is ambiguous, but the context is unambiguous.
'en associant à l'espace X, le genre (S, 𝔏), où 𝔏 est le filtre trivial sur S': the image appears to have X and S mixed; the intended sense is the germ (X, {X}) with the trivial filter on X.
'la cat. fibrée des revêtements de genres d'espaces induite celle des rev. d'espaces topologiques' is likely 'induit celle des rev. d'espaces topologiques'.
'Si 𝔛 est connexe, donc Rev(𝔛) est galoisienne' could also read 'i.e. Rev(𝔛) est galoisienne'.
The struck-out first token 'S' before '𝔛' in 'Soit [-S-] 𝔛' and the struck 'Alors' are correctly noted.
